# Functional diversity {#functional-diversity}

The previous chapters used abundances and a phylogeny. Here we add the
functional layer: genome-inferred traits distilled from KEGG ortholog
annotations of the same 5,518 representative MAGs. Each MAG has a completeness
score between zero and one for every function-level trait in the
[distillR](https://github.com/anttonalberdi/distillR) biosynthesis and
degradation domains, such as nucleic acid biosynthesis or polysaccharide
degradation. We turn these traits into a functional distance between MAGs and
use it in [hilldiv3](https://alberdilab.github.io/hilldiv3/) to calculate
functional diversity and related metrics.

```{r functional_setup, include=FALSE}
stopifnot(requireNamespace("distillR", quietly = TRUE),
          requireNamespace("cluster", quietly = TRUE),
          identical(rownames(overview_abundance), genome_metadata$genome_id),
          identical(colnames(overview_abundance), sample_metadata$sample_id))

plain_result <- function(x) {
  class(x) <- "data.frame"
  x
}
```

## Functional traits

`scripts/distill-functional-traits.R` distils the primary KEGG ortholog hit of
every gene (Drakkar 2.6.9, KOfam database of 2026-07-02) into trait tables. We
use the function level, which has one column per function and the same row
order as the representative metadata.

```{r functional_traits, message=FALSE}
functional_traits <- data.table::fread(
  cmd = "xz -dc data/mag_gift_functions.tsv.xz",
  data.table = FALSE, check.names = FALSE
)
stopifnot(identical(functional_traits$genome_id, genome_metadata$genome_id))
rownames(functional_traits) <- functional_traits$genome_id
functional_traits$genome_id <- NULL

# Protein degradation is defined by MEROPS peptidase families, which KEGG
# annotation cannot supply, so it is zero in every MAG and carries no signal.
empty_functions <- colnames(functional_traits)[colSums(functional_traits) == 0]
functional_traits <- functional_traits[, !colnames(functional_traits) %in%
                                         empty_functions, drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(identical(empty_functions, "D04"),
          all(as.matrix(functional_traits) >= 0 &
                as.matrix(functional_traits) <= 1))

function_labels <- unique(distillR::GIFT_db[c("Code_function", "Function",
                                              "Domain")])
function_labels <- function_labels[match(colnames(functional_traits),
                                         function_labels$Code_function), ]
stopifnot(!anyNA(function_labels$Function))
cat(sprintf("%d MAGs, %d function-level traits (%d biosynthesis, %d degradation).\n",
            nrow(functional_traits), ncol(functional_traits),
            sum(function_labels$Domain == "Biosynthesis"),
            sum(function_labels$Domain == "Degradation")))
```

## Functional distance

`traits2dist()` converts the trait table to a Gower distance, the mean absolute
difference in completeness across traits, scaled to the range of each trait.
Two MAGs with identical traits are at distance zero.

```{r functional_distance, class.source='script-source hilldiv3-source'}
functional_dist <- hilldiv3::traits2dist(functional_traits, method = "gower")
```

```{r functional_distance_summary}
stopifnot(identical(dim(functional_dist), c(5518L, 5518L)),
          all(is.finite(functional_dist)))
dimnames(functional_dist) <- list(genome_metadata$genome_id,
                                  genome_metadata$genome_id)
pair_distance <- functional_dist[upper.tri(functional_dist)]
distance_quantiles <- stats::quantile(pair_distance,
                                      c(0.01, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.99, 1))
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(Statistic = c("1%", "25%", "Median", "75%", "99%", "Maximum"),
             Distance = unname(distance_quantiles)),
  digits = 3
)
```

*Quantiles of the pairwise functional distance between the 5,518
representatives.*

Functional Hill numbers count the effective number of functionally distinct
types in a sample. Two MAGs closer than a threshold $\tau$ count as largely the
same type. We set $\tau$ to the mean pairwise distance,
`r sprintf("%.2f", mean(pair_distance))`, and examine how sensitive the results
are to this choice below.

```{r functional_tau}
functional_tau <- mean(pair_distance)
```

## Functional diversity within samples

We calculate neutral and functional Hill numbers at $q=0$, $q=1$ and $q=2$ from
the same abundances. A `dist` supplied with `type = "functional"` adds the
functional layer.

```{r functional_alpha_hilldiv, message=FALSE, class.source='script-source hilldiv3-source'}
fd_neutral <- hilldiv3::hilldiv(
  overview_abundance, q = c(0, 1, 2), type = "neutral"
)
fd_functional <- hilldiv3::hilldiv(
  overview_abundance, q = c(0, 1, 2), dist = functional_dist,
  tau = functional_tau, type = "functional"
)
```

```{r functional_alpha_data, include=FALSE}
fd_neutral <- plain_result(fd_neutral)
fd_functional <- plain_result(fd_functional)
fd_neutral$type <- "Neutral"
fd_functional$type <- "Functional"
fd_alpha <- rbind(fd_neutral, fd_functional)
fd_alpha$habitat <- sample_metadata$habitat_label[
  match(fd_alpha$sample, sample_metadata$sample_id)
]
stopifnot(!anyNA(fd_alpha$habitat), all(is.finite(fd_alpha$value)),
          all(fd_alpha$value > 0))
fd_alpha$habitat <- factor(fd_alpha$habitat, levels = rev(habitat_levels))
fd_alpha$type <- factor(fd_alpha$type, levels = c("Neutral", "Functional"))
fd_alpha$order <- factor(fd_alpha$q, levels = c(0, 1, 2),
                         labels = c("q = 0", "q = 1", "q = 2"))
```

```{r functional_alpha_plot, fig.width=11, fig.height=7.5, fig.alt="Boxplots and sample points for neutral and functional Hill diversity at orders 0, 1, and 2 across eight habitats."}
ggplot2::ggplot(fd_alpha, ggplot2::aes(x = value, y = habitat, fill = type)) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.55, alpha = 0.55,
                        colour = "grey20") +
  ggplot2::geom_jitter(height = 0.13, width = 0, alpha = 0.28,
                       size = 0.65, colour = "grey25") +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = type_colours, guide = "none") +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(ggplot2::vars(type, order), ncol = 3,
                      scales = "free_x") +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Hill diversity", y = NULL) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
                 strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"))
```

*Neutral and functional Hill numbers for 45 samples in each habitat class.
Horizontal scales differ by panel.*

```{r functional_alpha_summary}
fd_q1 <- fd_alpha[fd_alpha$q == 1, ]
fd_wide <- reshape(
  fd_q1[c("sample", "habitat", "type", "value")], idvar = c("sample", "habitat"),
  timevar = "type", direction = "wide"
)
names(fd_wide) <- sub("value\\.", "", names(fd_wide))
fd_wide$Redundancy <- fd_wide$Neutral / fd_wide$Functional
fd_summary <- function(x) {
  sprintf("%.1f [%.1f–%.1f]", median(x), unname(quantile(x, 0.25)),
          unname(quantile(x, 0.75)))
}
fd_table <- data.frame(
  Habitat = habitat_levels,
  Neutral = tapply(fd_wide$Neutral, fd_wide$habitat, fd_summary)[habitat_levels],
  Functional = tapply(fd_wide$Functional, fd_wide$habitat,
                      fd_summary)[habitat_levels],
  Redundancy = tapply(fd_wide$Redundancy, fd_wide$habitat,
                      fd_summary)[habitat_levels]
)
rownames(fd_table) <- NULL
knitr::kable(fd_table, col.names = c("Habitat", "Neutral q = 1",
                                     "Functional q = 1",
                                     "Functional redundancy"))
```

*Median [interquartile range] of $q=1$ diversity by habitat. Functional
redundancy is neutral divided by functional diversity: the number of effective
MAGs per effective functional type.*

```{r functional_alpha_interpretation, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
fd_medians <- tapply(fd_wide$Functional, fd_wide$habitat, median)
cat(sprintf(
  "At $q=1$, median functional diversity ranges from %.1f in %s to %.1f in %s, while neutral diversity ranges from %.0f to %.0f effective MAGs.\n\n",
  min(fd_medians), names(which.min(fd_medians)),
  max(fd_medians), names(which.max(fd_medians)),
  min(tapply(fd_wide$Neutral, fd_wide$habitat, median)),
  max(tapply(fd_wide$Neutral, fd_wide$habitat, median))
))
```

## Sensitivity to the distance threshold

Functional Hill numbers depend on $\tau$. A small $\tau$ treats nearly every
MAG as distinct and approaches neutral diversity; a large $\tau$ merges them
into a few functional types. We repeat the $q=1$ calculation across a range of
thresholds.

```{r functional_tau_sensitivity, message=FALSE, class.source='script-source hilldiv3-source'}
tau_values <- sort(unique(c(0.1, 0.15, functional_tau, 0.3, 0.4)))
tau_results <- lapply(tau_values, function(tau) {
  res <- plain_result(hilldiv3::hilldiv(
    overview_abundance, q = 1, dist = functional_dist, tau = tau,
    type = "functional"
  ))
  res$tau <- tau
  res
})
```

```{r functional_tau_plot, fig.width=9, fig.height=5.5, fig.alt="Median functional Hill diversity at order one against the distance threshold, one line per habitat."}
tau_data <- do.call(rbind, tau_results)
tau_data$habitat <- sample_metadata$habitat_label[
  match(tau_data$sample, sample_metadata$sample_id)
]
stopifnot(!anyNA(tau_data$habitat), all(is.finite(tau_data$value)))
tau_median <- aggregate(value ~ habitat + tau, data = tau_data, FUN = median)
tau_median$habitat <- factor(tau_median$habitat, levels = habitat_levels)
ggplot2::ggplot(tau_median,
                ggplot2::aes(x = tau, y = value, colour = habitat)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 1.2) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = functional_tau, linetype = "dashed",
                      colour = "grey40") +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = habitat_colours) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_log10() +
  ggplot2::labs(x = expression("Distance threshold" ~ tau),
                y = "Median functional Hill diversity, q = 1 (log scale)",
                colour = "Habitat") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank())
```

*Median functional diversity per habitat across thresholds. The dashed line is
the mean pairwise distance used elsewhere in this chapter.*

```{r functional_tau_interpretation, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
rank_by_tau <- vapply(tau_values, function(tau) {
  d <- tau_median[tau_median$tau == tau, ]
  as.character(d$habitat[which.max(d$value)])
}, "")
cat(sprintf(
  "The habitat with the highest median functional diversity is %s at %s of the %d thresholds tested.\n\n",
  names(sort(table(rank_by_tau), decreasing = TRUE))[1],
  max(table(rank_by_tau)), length(tau_values)
))
```

## Community-level trait profiles

The abundance-weighted mean completeness of each function in a sample, the
community-weighted mean (CWM), describes the average functional capacity of the
community without any threshold. It weights each MAG by its relative abundance
within the profile.

```{r functional_cwm}
relative_profiles <- sweep(overview_abundance, 2, colSums(overview_abundance),
                           "/")
cwm <- t(relative_profiles) %*% as.matrix(functional_traits)
stopifnot(identical(rownames(cwm), sample_metadata$sample_id),
          all(cwm >= -1e-10 & cwm <= 1 + 1e-10))
cwm_habitat <- aggregate(as.data.frame(cwm),
                         by = list(habitat = sample_metadata$habitat_label),
                         FUN = mean)
cwm_long <- reshape(
  cwm_habitat, direction = "long", idvar = "habitat",
  varying = colnames(cwm), v.names = "cwm", timevar = "code",
  times = colnames(cwm)
)
cwm_long$label <- paste(cwm_long$code,
                        function_labels$Function[match(cwm_long$code,
                                                       function_labels$Code_function)])
cwm_long$domain <- function_labels$Domain[match(cwm_long$code,
                                                function_labels$Code_function)]
cwm_long$habitat <- factor(cwm_long$habitat, levels = habitat_levels)
```

```{r functional_cwm_plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=8, fig.alt="Heat map of habitat mean community-weighted trait completeness for each function, split into biosynthesis and degradation."}
ggplot2::ggplot(cwm_long, ggplot2::aes(x = habitat, y = label, fill = cwm)) +
  ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", cwm)), size = 2.6) +
  ggplot2::facet_grid(rows = ggplot2::vars(domain), scales = "free_y",
                      space = "free_y") +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient(low = "#ffffff", high = "#c9784a",
                               limits = c(0, 1)) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(guide = ggplot2::guide_axis(angle = 35)) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Mean CWM\ncompleteness") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  ggplot2::theme(panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(),
                 strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"))
```

*Mean community-weighted completeness of each function across the 45 samples of
a habitat. Values range from zero (no MAG carries the function) to one (the
community is dominated by MAGs with the complete function).*

```{r functional_cwm_interpretation, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cwm_range <- tapply(cwm_long$cwm, cwm_long$label,
                    function(v) max(v) - min(v))
top_label <- names(which.max(cwm_range))
top_rows <- cwm_long[cwm_long$label == top_label, ]
cat(sprintf(
  "The function that differs most between habitats is %s, from %.2f in %s to %.2f in %s.\n\n",
  top_label, min(top_rows$cwm), top_rows$habitat[which.min(top_rows$cwm)],
  max(top_rows$cwm), top_rows$habitat[which.max(top_rows$cwm)]
))
```

## Partitioning functional diversity

`hillpart()` partitions functional diversity across samples, habitat classes
and the full panel, as for neutral and phylogenetic diversity in the
[diversity chapter](#diversity).

```{r functional_hillpart, message=FALSE, class.source='script-source hilldiv3-source'}
functional_metadata <- data.frame(
  habitat_class = sample_metadata$habitat_class,
  row.names = sample_metadata$sample_id
)
partition_functional <- hilldiv3::hillpart(
  overview_abundance, q = c(0, 1, 2), dist = functional_dist,
  tau = functional_tau, hierarchy = ~ habitat_class,
  metadata = functional_metadata, type = "functional"
)
```

```{r functional_partition_table}
partition_functional <- plain_result(partition_functional)
stopifnot(all(is.finite(partition_functional$diversity)))
f_within <- partition_functional[partition_functional$scale == "habitat_class",
                                 c("q", "beta")]
f_total <- partition_functional[partition_functional$scale == "total",
                                c("q", "beta", "diversity")]
f_alpha <- partition_functional[partition_functional$scale == "sample",
                                c("q", "diversity")]
names(f_alpha)[2] <- "Alpha diversity"
names(f_within)[2] <- "Within habitats"
names(f_total)[2:3] <- c("Between habitats", "Gamma diversity")
partition_functional_table <- Reduce(function(a, b) merge(a, b, by = "q"),
                                     list(f_alpha, f_within, f_total))
knitr::kable(partition_functional_table, digits = 2)
```

*Hierarchical partition of functional Hill numbers. Beta factors describe
sample-to-habitat and habitat-to-panel turnover.*

At $q=1$ the functional beta factors are
`r sprintf("%.2f", partition_functional_table[["Within habitats"]][partition_functional_table$q == 1])`
from samples to habitats and
`r sprintf("%.2f", partition_functional_table[["Between habitats"]][partition_functional_table$q == 1])`
from habitats to the full panel. These are much closer to one than the
neutral and phylogenetic factors: communities in different habitats consist of
different MAGs but carry largely overlapping functions.

## Pairwise functional dissimilarity

`hillpair()` compares every pair of samples, using the functional layer. As in
the [pairwise chapter](#pairwise-beta), we use the C dissimilarity, here at
$q=1$.

```{r functional_hillpair, message=FALSE, class.source='script-source hilldiv3-source'}
pair_functional <- hilldiv3::hillpair(
  overview_abundance, q = 1, metric = "C", dist = functional_dist,
  tau = functional_tau, type = "functional", out = "tibble"
)
```

```{r functional_pair_setup}
pair_functional <- plain_result(pair_functional)
fd_ids <- sample_metadata$sample_id
fd_first <- match(pair_functional$first, fd_ids)
fd_second <- match(pair_functional$second, fd_ids)
stopifnot(nrow(pair_functional) == choose(length(fd_ids), 2L),
          !anyNA(fd_first), !anyNA(fd_second), all(fd_first < fd_second),
          all(is.finite(pair_functional$value)),
          all(pair_functional$value >= -1e-10 &
                pair_functional$value <= 1 + 1e-10))
pair_functional$comparison <- ifelse(
  sample_metadata$habitat_label[fd_first] ==
    sample_metadata$habitat_label[fd_second],
  "Within habitat", "Between habitats"
)
pair_summary <- aggregate(
  value ~ comparison, data = pair_functional,
  FUN = function(x) sprintf("%.2f [%.2f–%.2f]", median(x),
                            unname(quantile(x, 0.25)),
                            unname(quantile(x, 0.75)))
)
knitr::kable(pair_summary, col.names = c("Pairs", "Functional C, q = 1"),
             row.names = FALSE)
```

*Median [interquartile range] of functional C dissimilarity. Zero means
identical functional communities and one means no functional overlap.*

```{r functional_ordination_data, include=FALSE}
fd_dist_matrix <- matrix(0, length(fd_ids), length(fd_ids),
                         dimnames = list(fd_ids, fd_ids))
fd_dist_matrix[cbind(fd_first, fd_second)] <- pair_functional$value
fd_dist_matrix[cbind(fd_second, fd_first)] <- pair_functional$value
fd_ord <- stats::cmdscale(stats::as.dist(fd_dist_matrix), k = 2, eig = TRUE,
                          add = TRUE)
fd_variance <- 100 * fd_ord$eig[1:2] / sum(pmax(fd_ord$eig, 0))
fd_points <- data.frame(
  sample_id = fd_ids,
  habitat = factor(sample_metadata$habitat_label, levels = habitat_levels),
  PCoA1 = fd_ord$points[, 1], PCoA2 = fd_ord$points[, 2]
)
stopifnot(all(is.finite(fd_ord$points)))
```

```{r functional_ordination, fig.width=8, fig.height=6.5, fig.alt="Principal coordinates plot of functional C dissimilarity at order one among 360 samples, coloured by habitat."}
ggplot2::ggplot(fd_points,
                ggplot2::aes(x = PCoA1, y = PCoA2, colour = habitat)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(alpha = 0.75, size = 1.5) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = habitat_colours) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = sprintf("PCoA 1 (%.1f%%)", fd_variance[1]),
                y = sprintf("PCoA 2 (%.1f%%)", fd_variance[2]),
                colour = "Habitat") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank())
```

*Each point is one sample. Axis percentages are the shares of positive
eigenvalues after the Cailliez correction.*

## Functional view of the Actinomycetota turnover

The [shares chapter](#shares) found a nearly stable Actinomycetota total in
agricultural field and natural grassland soils, with more Gaiellales in fields
and more Streptosporangiales in grasslands. Do these two orders carry different
functions, so that the swap changes what the community can do? We answer at the
finer **element** level, such as individual amino acids, sugars or vitamins,
which resolves more than the 17 function-level traits above.

```{r actino_functional_setup, message=FALSE}
element_traits <- data.table::fread(
  cmd = "xz -dc data/mag_gift_elements.tsv.xz",
  data.table = FALSE, check.names = FALSE
)
stopifnot(identical(element_traits$genome_id, genome_metadata$genome_id))
rownames(element_traits) <- element_traits$genome_id
element_traits$genome_id <- NULL
element_traits <- element_traits[, colSums(element_traits) > 0, drop = FALSE]
element_matrix <- as.matrix(element_traits)

element_labels <- unique(distillR::GIFT_db[c("Code_element", "Element",
                                             "Function")])
element_labels <- element_labels[match(colnames(element_matrix),
                                       element_labels$Code_element), ]
element_labels$label <- sprintf("%s %s (%s)", element_labels$Code_element,
                                element_labels$Element,
                                tolower(element_labels$Function))
stopifnot(!anyNA(element_labels$Element))

element_dist <- hilldiv3::traits2dist(element_traits, method = "gower")
dimnames(element_dist) <- list(genome_metadata$genome_id,
                               genome_metadata$genome_id)
element_tau <- mean(element_dist[upper.tri(element_dist)])
```

`traits2dist()` now uses the `r ncol(element_matrix)` of 170 elements that are
present in at least one MAG (the others, including the protein-degradation
elements, are absent from every MAG). We again set $\tau$ to the mean pairwise
distance,
`r sprintf("%.2f", element_tau)`.

The four disjoint sets are the two orders, the remaining Actinomycetota, and
everything outside the phylum. They cover all representatives, so contributions
add up to the total. We compare the mean field and grassland profiles, as in
the dissimilarity analysis of the shares chapter.

```{r actino_functional_sets}
actino_ids <- genome_metadata$genome_id[phylum == "Actinomycetota"]
fa_sets <- lapply(actino_orders, function(name) {
  actino_ids[genome_metadata[match(actino_ids, genome_metadata$genome_id),
                             "order"] == paste0("o__", name)]
})
names(fa_sets) <- actino_orders
fa_sets[["Remaining Actinomycetota"]] <- setdiff(actino_ids,
                                                 unlist(fa_sets))
fa_sets[["Outside Actinomycetota"]] <- setdiff(genome_metadata$genome_id,
                                               actino_ids)
stopifnot(all(lengths(fa_sets) > 0L),
          sum(lengths(fa_sets)) == nrow(genome_metadata),
          setequal(unlist(fa_sets, use.names = FALSE),
                   genome_metadata$genome_id))

fa_profiles <- function(field, grassland) {
  out <- cbind(rowMeans(overview_abundance[, field, drop = FALSE]),
               rowMeans(overview_abundance[, grassland, drop = FALSE]))
  colnames(out) <- contrast_habitats
  out
}
fa_field <- sample_metadata$habitat_label == contrast_habitats[1]
fa_grass <- sample_metadata$habitat_label == contrast_habitats[2]
fa_matched <- sample_metadata$project_id %in% c("P01_1", "P02_1")
```

### Functional dissimilarity and the contribution of each set

`hillcontrib()` splits the $q=1$ C dissimilarity between the two mean profiles
into contributions from each set. Neutral dissimilarity uses abundances alone;
functional dissimilarity adds the element distance, so MAGs with similar
elements count as the same functional type.

```{r actino_functional_contrib, message=FALSE, class.source='script-source hilldiv3-source'}
fa_mean <- fa_profiles(fa_field, fa_grass)
fa_neutral <- hilldiv3::hillcontrib(
  fa_mean, q = 1, metric = "C", type = "neutral", sets = fa_sets
)
fa_functional <- hilldiv3::hillcontrib(
  fa_mean, q = 1, metric = "C", dist = element_dist, tau = element_tau,
  type = "functional", sets = fa_sets
)
```

```{r actino_functional_summary, include=FALSE}
fa_neutral <- plain_result(fa_neutral)
fa_functional <- plain_result(fa_functional)
fa_orders_share <- function(x) {
  sum(x$share[x$set %in% actino_orders])
}

# Element-level split of the field-minus-grassland difference in
# community-weighted mean completeness; it sums exactly across sets.
fa_decompose <- function(profiles, sets = fa_sets) {
  weights <- sweep(profiles, 2, colSums(profiles), "/")
  delta <- weights[, 1] - weights[, 2]
  by_set <- vapply(sets, function(ids) {
    drop(crossprod(delta[ids], element_matrix[ids, , drop = FALSE]))
  }, numeric(ncol(element_matrix)))
  rownames(by_set) <- colnames(element_matrix)
  by_set
}

fa_check <- function(label, field, grassland, tau,
                     keep = rep(TRUE, nrow(genome_metadata))) {
  # MAGs outside `keep` get zero abundance and leave their sets.
  profiles <- fa_profiles(field, grassland)
  profiles[!keep, ] <- 0
  sets <- lapply(fa_sets, function(ids) {
    ids[keep[match(ids, genome_metadata$genome_id)]]
  })
  neutral <- plain_result(hilldiv3::hillcontrib(
    profiles, q = 1, metric = "C", type = "neutral", sets = sets
  ))
  functional <- plain_result(hilldiv3::hillcontrib(
    profiles, q = 1, metric = "C", dist = element_dist, tau = tau,
    type = "functional", sets = sets
  ))
  by_set <- fa_decompose(profiles, sets)
  g <- by_set[, "Gaiellales"]
  s <- by_set[, "Streptosporangiales"]
  data.frame(
    Comparison = label,
    neutral = sum(neutral$contribution),
    functional = sum(functional$contribution),
    share_neutral = fa_orders_share(neutral),
    share_functional = fa_orders_share(functional),
    correlation = stats::cor(g, s),
    offset = (sum(abs(g)) + sum(abs(s))) / sum(abs(g + s))
  )
}
# MAGs with CheckM2 completeness of at least 80% and contamination of at most
# 10%; incomplete MAGs lower trait completeness for technical reasons.
quality_keep <- genome_metadata$checkm2_completeness >= 80 &
  genome_metadata$checkm2_contamination <= 10
fa_robust <- rbind(
  fa_check("All samples, mean tau", fa_field, fa_grass, element_tau),
  fa_check("All samples, tau = 0.10", fa_field, fa_grass, 0.1),
  fa_check("All samples, tau = 0.40", fa_field, fa_grass, 0.4),
  fa_check("Project-matched samples, mean tau", fa_field & fa_matched,
           fa_grass & fa_matched, element_tau),
  fa_check("Higher-quality MAGs only, mean tau", fa_field, fa_grass,
           element_tau, keep = quality_keep)
)
stopifnot(
  sum(fa_field & fa_matched) == 16L, sum(fa_grass & fa_matched) == 7L,
  all(is.finite(as.matrix(fa_robust[-1]))),
  all(fa_robust$share_functional > fa_robust$share_neutral),
  all(fa_robust$correlation < 0), all(fa_robust$offset > 1)
)
```

```{r actino_functional_contrib_plot, fig.width=9, fig.height=3.8, fig.alt="Two stacked bars divide neutral and functional C dissimilarity between mean agricultural field and natural grassland soil profiles among Gaiellales, Streptosporangiales, the remaining Actinomycetota and everything outside the phylum."}
fa_plot <- rbind(
  data.frame(type = "Neutral", fa_neutral[c("set", "share")]),
  data.frame(type = "Functional (elements)", fa_functional[c("set", "share")])
)
fa_plot$set <- factor(fa_plot$set, levels = rev(c(
  actino_orders, "Remaining Actinomycetota", "Outside Actinomycetota"
)))
fa_plot$type <- factor(fa_plot$type,
                       levels = c("Neutral", "Functional (elements)"))
ggplot2::ggplot(fa_plot, ggplot2::aes(x = share, y = type, fill = set)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(width = 0.6, colour = "white") +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    Gaiellales = "#B79F2B", Streptosporangiales = "#7A6A1F",
    `Remaining Actinomycetota` = "#EFE7BC",
    `Outside Actinomycetota` = "#BBBBBB"
  ), breaks = c(actino_orders, "Remaining Actinomycetota",
                "Outside Actinomycetota")) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent()) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Share of C dissimilarity", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
                 legend.position = "bottom")
```

*Share of the $q=1$ C dissimilarity between mean field and grassland profiles
attributed to each set, for abundance alone (neutral) and with the element
distance (functional).*

Neutral C between the two mean profiles is
`r sprintf("%.3f", fa_robust$neutral[1])`, while functional C is only
`r sprintf("%.3f", fa_robust$functional[1])` at this threshold: most of the
abundance turnover replaces MAGs with similar elements. Gaiellales and Streptosporangiales hold
only
`r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * sum(lengths(fa_sets[actino_orders])) / nrow(genome_metadata))`
of the representatives, yet they account for
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * fa_robust$share_neutral[1])`
of the neutral and
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * fa_robust$share_functional[1])`
of the functional dissimilarity. The two orders therefore explain a larger part
of the functional turnover than of the abundance turnover.

```{r actino_functional_robust_table}
fa_robust_table <- data.frame(
  fa_robust$Comparison,
  sprintf("%.3f", fa_robust$neutral),
  sprintf("%.3f", fa_robust$functional),
  sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * fa_robust$share_neutral),
  sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * fa_robust$share_functional)
)
knitr::kable(fa_robust_table, col.names = c(
  "Comparison", "Neutral C", "Functional C",
  "Orders' share of neutral C", "Orders' share of functional C"
))
```

*Functional dissimilarity depends on $\tau$ (a small threshold approaches the
neutral value, a large one removes it), so it is shown for three thresholds,
for the 16 field and 7 grassland samples that share projects, as in the shares
chapter, and for MAGs with CheckM2 completeness of at least 80% and
contamination of at most 10%. The orders' larger share of functional
dissimilarity holds in every row, but its margin is smallest among the
higher-quality MAGs.*

### Do the two orders offset each other?

For each element we split the field-minus-grassland difference in
community-weighted mean completeness into the part contributed by each set.
Positive values mean higher completeness in fields. If the swap between orders
left the community's functions unchanged, Gaiellales and Streptosporangiales
would contribute opposite amounts for every element.

```{r actino_functional_decomposition}
fa_by_set <- fa_decompose(fa_mean)
fa_elements <- data.frame(
  code = rownames(fa_by_set), fa_by_set, check.names = FALSE,
  label = element_labels$label[match(rownames(fa_by_set),
                                     element_labels$Code_element)]
)
fa_elements$orders <- fa_elements$Gaiellales + fa_elements$Streptosporangiales
fa_elements$total <- rowSums(fa_by_set)
stopifnot(!anyNA(fa_elements$label))
fa_top <- fa_elements[order(-abs(fa_elements$orders)), ][1:12, ]
```

```{r actino_functional_scatter, fig.width=7, fig.height=6, fig.alt="Scatter plot of the Gaiellales contribution against the Streptosporangiales contribution to the field-minus-grassland difference in mean element completeness; points lie along a descending line."}
ggplot2::ggplot(fa_elements,
                ggplot2::aes(x = Gaiellales, y = Streptosporangiales)) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey70") +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey70") +
  ggplot2::geom_abline(slope = -1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed",
                       colour = "grey40") +
  ggplot2::geom_point(colour = type_colours[["Functional"]], alpha = 0.7, size = 1.6) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Gaiellales contribution",
                y = "Streptosporangiales contribution") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank())
```

*Each point is one element. The dashed line marks complete offset: the two
orders contribute equal and opposite amounts.*

The contributions of the two orders are negatively correlated across the
`r nrow(fa_elements)` elements (r = `r sprintf("%.2f", fa_robust$correlation[1])`).
Summed over elements, their absolute contributions are
`r sprintf("%.1f", fa_robust$offset[1])` times larger than the absolute
contribution of the two orders combined, so most of what one order adds is
cancelled by the other. The offset is partial: the two orders together still
shift the completeness of individual elements.

```{r actino_functional_top_plot, fig.width=9, fig.height=5.5, fig.alt="For the twelve elements with the largest combined effect of the two orders, bars show the Gaiellales and Streptosporangiales contributions to the field-minus-grassland difference in mean completeness and a point shows their sum."}
fa_top_long <- rbind(
  data.frame(label = fa_top$label, set = "Gaiellales",
             value = fa_top$Gaiellales),
  data.frame(label = fa_top$label, set = "Streptosporangiales",
             value = fa_top$Streptosporangiales)
)
fa_top_long$label <- factor(fa_top_long$label, levels = rev(fa_top$label))
fa_top$label <- factor(fa_top$label, levels = rev(fa_top$label))
ggplot2::ggplot(fa_top_long, ggplot2::aes(x = value, y = label)) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey70") +
  ggplot2::geom_col(ggplot2::aes(fill = set), position = "dodge",
                    width = 0.7) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(data = fa_top, ggplot2::aes(x = orders, y = label),
                      shape = 18, size = 3) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = c(Gaiellales = "#B79F2B",
                                        Streptosporangiales = "#7A6A1F")) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Contribution to field minus grassland mean completeness",
                y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
                 legend.position = "bottom")
```

*The twelve elements with the largest net effect of the two orders. Bars are the
contribution of each order; the diamond is their sum.*

```{r actino_functional_top_text, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
lead <- fa_top[1, ]
cat(sprintf(
  "The largest net effect is for %s: Gaiellales contributes %+.3f and Streptosporangiales %+.3f, so the orders together shift it by %+.3f.\n\n",
  lead$label, lead$Gaiellales, lead$Streptosporangiales, lead$orders
))
```

Of these `r nrow(fa_top)` elements,
`r sum(grepl("^D", fa_top$code) & fa_top$Streptosporangiales < 0)` are
degradation elements for which Streptosporangiales, enriched in grasslands,
raises grassland completeness. The replacement of Gaiellales by
Streptosporangiales is therefore not functionally neutral at the level of
individual elements, even though the overall functional dissimilarity is small.

## Trait validation and sensitivity to MAG quality

Before relying on the traits we check that they behave as expected for clades
whose metabolism is well known, and that the main results do not simply track
how complete a MAG is.

```{r functional_validation}
validation_phyla <- names(which(table(phylum) >= 60L))
validation_codes <- c("B01", "B02", "B07", "D02")
validation <- t(vapply(validation_phyla, function(name) {
  colMeans(functional_traits[phylum == name, validation_codes])
}, numeric(length(validation_codes))))
validation <- validation[order(-validation[, "D02"]), ]
antibiotic_max <- max(vapply(validation_phyla, function(name) {
  mean(functional_traits[phylum == name, "B10"])
}, numeric(1)))
stopifnot(antibiotic_max < 0.05)
colnames(validation) <- function_labels$Function[
  match(validation_codes, function_labels$Code_function)
]
knitr::kable(validation, digits = 2)
```

*Mean completeness of four functions among the phyla with at least 60
representatives.*

The patterns match expectations. Patescibacteria, whose reduced genomes depend
on other cells, score near zero for amino acid
(`r sprintf("%.2f", validation["Patescibacteria", "Amino acid biosynthesis"])`)
and vitamin
(`r sprintf("%.2f", validation["Patescibacteria", "Vitamin biosynthesis"])`)
biosynthesis, and well below the other phyla for nucleic acids
(`r sprintf("%.2f", validation["Patescibacteria", "Nucleic acid biosynthesis"])`
against at least
`r sprintf("%.2f", min(validation[rownames(validation) != "Patescibacteria", "Nucleic acid biosynthesis"]))`).
Polysaccharide degradation is highest in
`r paste(head(rownames(validation), 3), collapse = ", ")`, groups known for
degrading complex carbohydrates, and lowest in
`r tail(rownames(validation), 1)`. KEGG orthologs do not resolve antibiotic
biosynthesis: it stays below 0.05 in every phylum, including the Actinomycetota.

```{r functional_quality, message=FALSE}
trait_cors <- vapply(c("genome_size", "checkm2_completeness"), function(v) {
  stats::median(abs(vapply(colnames(functional_traits), function(f) {
    stats::cor(functional_traits[[f]], genome_metadata[[v]],
               method = "spearman")
  }, numeric(1))))
}, numeric(1))
```

Trait completeness rises with genome size and CheckM2 completeness: the
median absolute Spearman correlation across the 17 functions is
`r sprintf("%.2f", trait_cors["genome_size"])` with genome size and
`r sprintf("%.2f", trait_cors["checkm2_completeness"])` with completeness.
Larger genomes do carry more metabolic functions, but incomplete MAGs also
miss genes, so trait values are lower bounds. To see whether the conclusions
depend on this, we repeat the analyses with the
`r sum(quality_keep)` representatives that have CheckM2 completeness of at
least 80% and contamination of at most 10%, renormalizing each profile.

```{r functional_quality_alpha, message=FALSE, class.source='script-source hilldiv3-source'}
quality_profiles <- overview_abundance[quality_keep, , drop = FALSE]
quality_profiles <- sweep(quality_profiles, 2, colSums(quality_profiles), "/")
quality_dist <- functional_dist[quality_keep, quality_keep]
quality_functional <- hilldiv3::hilldiv(
  quality_profiles, q = 1, dist = quality_dist,
  tau = mean(quality_dist[upper.tri(quality_dist)]), type = "functional"
)
```

```{r functional_quality_summary}
quality_functional <- plain_result(quality_functional)
quality_medians <- tapply(
  quality_functional$value,
  sample_metadata$habitat_label[match(quality_functional$sample,
                                      sample_metadata$sample_id)],
  median
)[habitat_levels]
all_medians <- tapply(fd_wide$Functional, fd_wide$habitat,
                      median)[habitat_levels]
quality_cwm <- t(quality_profiles) %*%
  as.matrix(functional_traits[quality_keep, ])
cwm_agreement <- vapply(colnames(cwm), function(f) {
  stats::cor(tapply(cwm[, f], sample_metadata$habitat_label,
                    mean)[habitat_levels],
             tapply(quality_cwm[, f], sample_metadata$habitat_label,
                    mean)[habitat_levels], method = "spearman")
}, numeric(1))
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(Habitat = habitat_levels,
             `All MAGs` = unname(all_medians),
             `Higher-quality MAGs` = unname(quality_medians),
             check.names = FALSE),
  digits = 2
)
```

*Median functional diversity ($q=1$) per habitat with all representatives and
with the higher-quality subset. Each uses its own mean pairwise distance as
$\tau$.*

```{r functional_quality_interpretation, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat(sprintf(
  "The subset holds a median of %.0f%% of each sample's profile. Absolute functional diversity is lower, but the habitat ranking is similar (Spearman %.2f) and %s remains highest. The habitat means of the community-weighted trait profiles agree between the two sets (median Spearman %.2f across functions, minimum %.2f).\n\n",
  100 * median(colSums(overview_abundance[quality_keep, , drop = FALSE])),
  stats::cor(all_medians, quality_medians, method = "spearman"),
  names(which.max(quality_medians)), median(cwm_agreement),
  min(cwm_agreement)
))
```

Within the Actinomycetota analysis, the higher-quality row of the robustness
table keeps the negative correlation between the orders
(r = `r sprintf("%.2f", fa_robust$correlation[nrow(fa_robust)])`) and a small
functional dissimilarity, but the orders' share of functional dissimilarity
falls to
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * fa_robust$share_functional[nrow(fa_robust)])`
against
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * fa_robust$share_neutral[nrow(fa_robust)])`
neutral. We therefore read that excess as a modest, not a large, effect.

## Interpretation and limits

These traits come from gene presence in KEGG ortholog annotations. They
describe genomic potential, not expressed activity, and cover only functions
that KEGG orthologs and EC numbers can define. Protein degradation, which needs
MEROPS peptidase families, is left out. Each representative's abundance stands
for its 95% ANI cluster, which need not share its gene content.

Functional diversity depends on the trait set and on $\tau$; compare values
only within one choice of both. The pairwise and ordination summaries describe
this selected panel. Pairs sharing samples are dependent, and habitat class is
partly confounded with sampling year, so none of these comparisons is a formal
test of a habitat effect. Relative abundances also cannot support read-count
rarefaction or sampling-depth uncertainty estimates.
